data.title: Knorex Announces Dec. 16 EGM on Share Consolidation and Capital Increase
data.description:
An update from Knorex Ltd Class A ( (KNRXF) ) is now available.

Knorex Ltd. is a Cayman Islands-incorporated issuer with Class A and Class B ordinary shares; the release does not identify its industry, primary products or services, or market focus. On November 27, 2026, the company announced a hybrid extraordinary general meeting for December 16, 2026, in Singapore, where shareholders will consider a proposed 1-for-100 consolidation of both share classes.

A proposal subject to the consolidation would increase authorized share capital from $50,000 divided into 1 million shares to $50 million divided into 1 billion shares. data.title: Halfords Earnings Call Shows Strong Growth Despite Caution
data.description:
Halfords Group plc ((GB:HFD)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Halfords delivered a strongly positive first-half performance, with gains in sales, margins, profit, cash generation and returns. Management raised full-year profit guidance and the interim dividend, although it cautioned that unusually warm weather will not recur, second-half margins may moderate and Avayler remains loss-making.

Strong First-Half Group Performance

Halfords increased like-for-like sales by 7.1%, while underlying operating margin rose 140 basis points to 4.6%. Underlying profit before tax jumped 66% to £39 million, and return on capital improved 530 basis points to 18.9%.

Underlying Growth Excluding Weather

After removing an estimated £8 million benefit from exceptionally warm weather, like-for-like sales still grew 5.6%. Underlying operating margin increased to 3.8%, profit before tax rose 31.9% to £31 million and return on capital remained comfortably above the cost of capital at 16.9%.

Revenue and Gross-Margin Expansion

Revenue climbed 6.7% to £953 million, while gross margin widened 120 basis points to 52.6%. Halfords attributed the improvement to effective pricing, promotional activity, favourable foreign exchange and a stronger mix of seasonal categories.

Operating Leverage Improves Profitability

Operating costs rose 6.2%, below the rate of revenue growth, showing the benefit of cost discipline and operating leverage. This was achieved despite wage and fuel inflation, higher incentive provisions and continued investment, helping underlying profit before tax rise from £23.5 million to £39 million.

Retail Sales and Profit Growth

Retail revenue increased 7.3% to £572 million, with like-for-like sales up 7.7%. Motoring grew 7.3% and cycling 8.3%, while retail operating profit rose 46.1% to £30.1 million and the margin improved from 3.9% to 5.3%.

Category Management Shows Early Gains

Wave One category-management trials covered about 15% of retail sales and included workshops, flagship cycling and cycling parts and accessories. The trialled categories delivered more than 5% growth in both sales and margin, supporting Halfords’ plan to relaunch about 60% of its ranges by the end of FY28.

Cycling and E-Bike Momentum

Cycling sales grew by more than 8%, with bikes and parts and accessories contributing broadly similar growth. Electric-bike sales rose 45% year on year, and e-bikes accounted for about one-quarter of all bikes sold.

Autocentres Growth and Margin Improvement

Excluding Avayler, Autocentres revenue rose 5.9% to £380.2 million, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.1%. Underlying operating profit increased by more than 60% to £16.1 million, lifting the operating margin from 2.8% to 4.2%.

Autocentres Productivity Advances

Autocentres reduced labour costs as a share of sales by more than 200 basis points, helped by improved garage utilisation. Additional work identified represented about one-quarter of consumer-garage revenue, while tyre market share and income per tyre also benefited from services such as wheel alignment and warranties.

Fusion Program Supports Garage Expansion

There were 121 Fusion sites trading, and the rollout remained on track for completion by the end of the financial year. The format typically pays back within two years, giving management confidence that the garages business can progress towards its medium-term 5% to 6% operating-margin goal.

Digital and Retail Services Develop

Group online sales grew by just under 6%, with 80% of online orders collected in stores. Services grew faster than product sales, supported by higher profit per job and particularly strong demand for bike servicing, repairs and dash-cam fitting.

Strong Cash Generation and Balance Sheet

Halfords generated £38 million of free cash flow and ended the period with net cash of £40.1 million. Including lease liabilities, net debt fell to £207 million from £228.7 million at the FY26 year-end, while the £180 million revolving credit facility remained undrawn.

Distribution Center Investment

Halfords has signed a lease for a new distribution center in Coventry, scheduled to open in FY30. The company plans to fund £40 million to £50 million of capital investment directly over the next three years, while £35 million to £45 million of related non-underlying operating costs will remain within existing guardrails.

Distribution Center Expected to Add Value

Management expects the new center to deliver low- to mid-teens millions of pounds in annual profit benefits once mature. Benefits are expected to begin in FY30 and build through FY32, while the project should improve customer service and colleague experience and generate returns well above the cost of capital.

Interim Dividend Increased

The Board declared an interim dividend of 3.5 pence per share, up from 3 pence in the comparable period. Halfords’ policy is to cover dividends by between 1.5 and 2.5 times profit after tax.

Investment in Brand and Capability

Halfords has begun investing in a new brand platform and is increasing spending on marketing, technology, data and colleague capability. Management said the additional investment is intended to support current momentum while strengthening the foundations for longer-term growth.

Resilient Footprint and B2B Revenue

All 366 retail stores were described as profitable, with no store-closure program planned, while the group operates just under 500 garages. About 30% of group revenue comes from business customers, including reliable and recurring fleet-service and MOT work.

Weather Benefit Will Not Be Repeated

Management estimated that the early, warm summer added around £8 million to underlying profit. It stressed that the same favourable weather and incremental earnings cannot be assumed in future periods, making the adjusted performance a more useful guide to underlying momentum.

Second-Half Margin Moderation Expected

First-half margins did not fully reflect the effect of higher oil prices, and Halfords expects margin growth to moderate in the second half. Retail also assumes no further improvement in the gross-margin rate after significant expansion during the past two years.

Inflation and Incentive Costs Rise

The group continues to face wage and fuel inflation, alongside substantially higher incentive costs. Strong first-half results increased the annual bonus provision, while the higher share price raised costs linked to long-term incentive awards.

Avayler Losses Remain a Concern

Avayler revenue was broadly stable, but its operating loss widened to £2.3 million as Halfords continued investing in the platform. External-customer revenue has taken longer to develop than expected, and management is reviewing the business during the second half.

Sales Growth Returns to Normal

Sales growth returned to more typical levels in October and November rather than matching the exceptional pace seen during the hot summer. Halfords also plans to reinvest part of the first-half outperformance into the second half.

Consumer and Market Volatility

Management highlighted risks from a more inflationary environment, sustained high oil prices and potentially higher energy costs. It also warned that weather, consumer confidence and wider industry conditions could create periods of volatility.

Retail Margin Progress May Be Uneven

Management cautioned that progress towards higher retail operating margins should not be expected to move in a straight line. The business must absorb further inflation while continuing to invest in its customer proposition and future growth.

Guidance and Outlook

Halfords raised FY27 underlying profit-before-tax guidance to £60 million-£65 million and expects performance to be weighted towards the first half. It expects second-half margin growth to moderate, targets medium-term operating margins of 5% to 6% in retail and garages, and plans the Coventry center for FY30, with mature annual benefits in the low to mid-teens of millions by FY32.

Halfords’ call combined strong operational delivery with a more measured outlook for the rest of the year. The raised guidance, dividend increase, robust balance sheet and investment pipeline are encouraging, but investors will watch weather normalization, cost pressures, margin progression and the outcome of the Avayler review.

Halfords Earnings Call Shows Strong Growth Despite Caution

data.title: Finvolution Group Earnings Call Shows Overseas Strength, China Strain
data.description:
Finvolution Group ((FINV)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Finvolution Group’s earnings call delivered a mixed message for investors. Overseas expansion, stronger profitability, liquidity and cost controls offered support, but a sharp China slowdown, weaker asset quality, higher funding costs and lower profit kept management cautious about the pace of recovery.

Revenue Growth Came From Overseas Diversification

Third-quarter revenue rose 11% year over year and 2% sequentially to RMB 949 million. Overseas operations contributed 37% of group revenue, helping offset weakness in the company’s domestic business.

Overseas Volume and Profitability Improved

Overseas loan volume increased 11% year over year to RMB 4 billion and rose 5% from the previous quarter. Overseas operating profit reached RMB 62 million, up 15% sequentially and more than double the year-earlier figure.

International Revenue Mix Passed Its Annual Target

Overseas revenue represented about 31% of total revenue during the first nine months, compared with approximately 20% in 2024 and 25% in 2025. That exceeded the company’s 30% annual target and supports its longer-term ambition to generate more than half of revenue internationally.

Overseas EBITDA Plan Remained on Track

Overseas operating profit totaled approximately RMB 161 million in the first nine months. All three overseas markets were profitable at the operating level and contributed USD 24 million, keeping the business on track for its full-year EBITDA objective.

Overseas Borrower Acquisition Accelerated

Finvolution added 2.8 million new overseas borrowers in the third quarter, a 28% increase from the previous quarter. The figure highlights the company’s continued ability to expand its international customer base despite challenging economic conditions.

Indonesia Expanded Offline Buy Now, Pay Later

Offline Buy Now, Pay Later accounted for about 31% of Indonesia’s third-quarter volume, up from 25% in the prior quarter and 10% a year earlier. Management said the point-of-sale model improves verification of fund use and relies more on merchant networks than paid traffic.

Australia Delivered Stronger Growth and Customer Quality

Australia’s volume rose 21% sequentially, while middle- and large-loan customers reached about half of the portfolio. Deeper open-banking integration and verified data on income, spending and existing debt supported the shift toward higher-quality borrowers.

Fundo Integration Strengthened Australia

Since the Fundo acquisition, Australian new borrowers more than doubled year over year in the third quarter, transaction volume increased nearly 80%, and loan balances doubled. Revenue rose about 50%, while profitability also improved substantially.

Australia Added Digital and Product Capacity

Medium- and large-sized loans represented 51% of Australia’s third-quarter mix, compared with 38% a year earlier. Finvolution’s own app generated 40% of originations, Fundo team retention was about 90%, and management highlighted continued work on products, digital experience and customer retention.

Philippines Credit Performance Beat Expectations

Philippines volume declined 5% sequentially as the business adjusted to a new rate cap, but credit performance was better than expected. Conservative underwriting over the past three quarters helped limit pressure, and management said the transition was largely complete.

China Funding Supply Began to Stabilize

China’s funding supply recovered steadily from its July low through August and September, then remained stable in October and November. Management said available funding had reached a level sufficient for the company’s current risk appetite and origination plan.

Compliance Work Supported Bank Relationships

The company worked with banks on compliant loan products and referral flows, while adding closed-loop payment controls and further checks. It also submitted clean independent audits of fund flows to China’s National Internet Finance Association, helping it remain credible as lenders became more selective.

AI Expanded Collection and Service Capacity

AI collection agents helped replace some capacity lost during an industry-wide campaign targeting collection agencies. Finvolution’s AI applications, including a customer-service agent built on its RAG Fin model, were recognized as exemplary Shanghai cases and have served more than 100 million users.

AI Improved Recovery Rates

For accounts overdue for longer periods, monthly recovery using AI was nearly 1.5 times the rate achieved by third-party collection agencies through phone calls. The result points to potential efficiency gains as the company manages credit losses and customer service at scale.

Liquidity Stayed Strong and Leverage Fell

Cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 8.4 billion at the end of the third quarter, or about USD 1.2 billion. The risk-bearing loan balance divided by shareholders’ equity was 1.5 times, which management described as a historical low.

Share Buybacks and Debt Reduction Continued

Finvolution repurchased USD 4.3 million of shares in the third quarter and USD 71.1 million in the first nine months, reducing shares outstanding by 5.8% from year-end. It also bought back about USD 19 million of convertible senior notes in October, lowering debt and potential dilution.

Operating Expenses Declined Sharply

Group operating expenses fell 27% sequentially to RMB 1.048 billion. Lower sales and marketing costs were the main driver, as the company served more repeat customers through its own app instead of relying as heavily on paid traffic.

Currency Exposure Was Partly Hedged

Management said local-currency assets are matched with local-currency liabilities in overseas markets. This structure is intended to limit the effect of currency movements on the group’s reported results.

China Credit Shock Disrupted Operations

A credit event at another platform in July weakened confidence across China’s loan-facilitation industry. A nationwide campaign against collection agencies that began in late July also reduced collection capacity and efficiency, affecting funding, credit performance and origination.

Group Loan Volume Fell 56%

Group loan volume dropped to approximately RMB 20 billion in the third quarter, down 56% sequentially. The decline was driven mainly by the severe slowdown in China, which outweighed growth in international markets.

China Loan Volume Contracted 61%

China loan volume fell to roughly RMB 16 billion, a 61% sequential decline. Tighter funding supply and elevated credit risk across the industry forced the company to reduce origination significantly.

China Revenue and Take Rate Declined

China revenue fell 38% sequentially to RMB 1.5 billion as the loan book shrank. The take rate declined 30 basis points to about 2.9%, reflecting higher credit and funding costs.

China Asset Quality Weakened

China’s day-one delinquency rate rose to 6.35% from 5.26% in the second quarter, while the 30-day collection rate fell to 85.5% from 89.4%. The CM2 flow rate increased to 0.92% from 0.56%, and the third-quarter vintage cost estimate climbed to 3.5%.

Legacy Loans Continued to Lift Credit Costs

Management expects older loans to remain a source of credit-cost pressure. Total provision expense was broadly flat at RMB 1.35 billion despite lower origination, because credit costs on legacy loans increased.

China Funding Costs Rose Further

China funding costs increased to about 4.3% in the third quarter from approximately 3.7% in the second quarter. Management indicated that costs would remain elevated in the fourth quarter and could move slightly above the third-quarter level.

China Volume Recovery Remained Uncertain

China transaction volume was down about 60% quarter over quarter, and management said funding had not returned to normal. Future volume will depend on loan quality and expected returns, with tight underwriting maintained for new borrowers.

Credit Risk Had Not Reached a Clear Turning Point

The CM2 flow rate fell 6% in October from September as the 30-day collection rate improved modestly. Management cautioned that the change was recent and that, because average loan tenure is eight to nine months, it can take two to three quarters for existing-book risk to work through the portfolio.

Domestic Net Profit Fell 52%

Group net revenue declined 25% sequentially to RMB 2.6 billion, while net profit fell 52% to RMB 206 million. The results reflected lower China origination, higher funding costs and rising credit pressure.

Philippines Volume Fell During the Rate-Cap Shift

Loan volume in the Philippines decreased 5% from the previous quarter as the business adapted to the new rate cap. Management said the adjustment period was largely complete, creating a basis for a measured return to growth.

Macroeconomic Pressure Covered All Overseas Markets

Management cited higher oil prices, inflation and tighter monetary policy across the region. Indonesia faced currency pressure and weaker consumer confidence, the Philippines saw inflation reach 7.2% in September, and Australia’s rate increases put additional pressure on household budgets.

Regulation and Geopolitics Remained Risks

Developing-market regulations can change quickly, and rate-cap changes may slow growth in the short term. Management also highlighted inflation, currency and geopolitical risks in Indonesia and the Philippines, requiring careful monitoring and flexible operating plans.

Guidance Pointed to a Cautious Near-Term Outlook

Finvolution reiterated full-year revenue guidance of RMB 11.5 billion to RMB 12.9 billion but expects to finish near the lower end of the range. Funding costs may remain slightly above third-quarter levels, while China volume recovery will depend on loan quality and returns; overseas EBITDA remains on track for about USD 30 million, with measured Philippines growth and continued Australia investment expected.

The earnings call showed a company with a growing and increasingly profitable international platform, strong liquidity and disciplined spending. Those positives were overshadowed by China’s sharp volume contraction and unresolved credit and funding issues, leaving the recovery story dependent on better asset quality and a gradual improvement in domestic conditions.

data.title: Nanoco Group Earnings Call Signals Progress Amid Risks
data.description:
Nanoco Group plc ((GB:NANO)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Nanoco Group’s earnings call carried a cautiously positive tone. Management highlighted a $5 million LG settlement, lower costs, a £6.2 million opening order book and progress with Asian customers, but the company remains loss-making, cash-burning and exposed to uncertain adoption, timing, customer concentration and technology risks.

Asian Customer Moves Toward Scale-Up

Nanoco has started a three-year joint development agreement with its first Asian chemical customer, which commits to minimum spending of about £0.5 million annually. The program is entering scale-up, with higher material demand expected over the next six months and testing now covering stability and heat stress.

Second Asian Development Agreement Completed

A one-year agreement with a second Asian chemical customer has been completed, also involving indium arsenide materials. Nanoco remains in discussions about a further agreement or additional material purchases, although customer confidentiality limits detail on end markets and supply chains.

Grant Targets and Lead Sulfide Research

Nanoco completed its Innovate UK grant on first-generation lead sulfide and met all project targets. It is continuing work on an internally developed one-step lead sulfide process, supporting its broader effort to improve quantum-dot materials.

LG Settlement Strengthens Intellectual Property Position

The company reached a $5 million settlement with LG Electronics and granted LG a license for display applications. Nanoco also settled with Shoei Chemical, including a covenant not to sue covering key areas of its intellectual property focus.

Product Sales Remain Small but Improved

Product sales were only £13,000 in FY2026, but had reached about £41,000 in FY2027 at the time of the presentation. Management attributed the improvement to business-development investment and continued work on quantum dots and materials that could improve existing technologies.

Lean Operating Structure Cuts Costs

Nanoco reduced its Board from seven members to three and cut headcount from 29 to 23, while retaining core research staff, who now represent more than half of employees. Premises were consolidated without disrupting research or indium arsenide scale-up, reducing cash costs by about £0.3 million a year.

Settlement Drives Better Financial Results

Revenue rose by £3.4 million year on year, largely because of the LG settlement, while adjusted EBITDA increased to £5.3 million from £0.8 million. The improvement reflected settlement income and incremental cost savings rather than a major increase in product sales.

Operating Loss Narrows

Normal operating costs, including cost of sales, research and development and administration, fell from £6.2 million to £5.2 million. The operating loss narrowed to £1.0 million from £2.3 million, while the loss after tax improved to £2.0 million from £2.8 million.

Opening Order Book Provides Visibility

Nanoco entered FY2027 with an opening order book of £6.2 million. This included £5.6 million linked to the release of the Samsung license and £0.6 million from joint development and material orders that had already been invoiced.

Two-Year Cash Runway

Gross cash costs remain broadly stable at £0.3 million to £0.4 million per month. Management said the company would have around two years of runway even with no cash revenue, supported by a low breakeven point and considerable operating leverage.

Investment Continues in Devices and IP

Nanoco plans to spend about £0.1 million on device capabilities and a further £0.1 million on intellectual property during the year. It also intends to test materials on silicon coupons and CMOS integration, with the goal of developing its own Level 3 sensor prototype in FY2027.

Shareholders Back Commercialization

In a shareholder consultation, 81% of respondents preferred cash to be directed toward commercializing technology rather than returned to investors. Investment returns and capital growth were the leading reasons for holding the shares, while 63% wanted Nanoco to remain listed.

Image Sensing Is the Main Priority

Nanoco identified quantum-dot-enabled image sensing as its priority market, bringing together its intellectual property, experience, customer relationships and commercial opportunity. Its four quantum-dot material sets cover wavelengths from near-infrared at 800 nanometers to mid-wave infrared at about 3,500 nanometers.

Heavy-Metal-Free Technology Offers Differentiation

The company presented itself as a pioneer in heavy-metal-free quantum dots, supported by a deep patent portfolio, technical know-how and paid development partnerships. Its materials are designed to be deposited directly onto standard CMOS chips, with potential volume sensor costs ranging from €10 to €100.

Wide Range of Sensor Applications

Management sees potential for short-wave infrared sensors in automotive systems, defense, security, LiDAR, robotics and under-display sensing. Other possible uses include material sorting, motion detection, wafer inspection and wider industrial applications.

Large Market Opportunity, But Timing Has Shifted

Nanoco cited a Yole Intelligence forecast for the short-wave infrared imaging market to grow from $322 million in 2022 to $2.9 billion by 2028. Management said the forecast is now dated and that reaching that scale around 2031 may be a more realistic assumption, although defense demand is already supporting growth.

Customer Pipeline Is Expanding

The company reported good global coverage of image-sensor opportunities and a pipeline of Asian customers targeting high-volume markets. It is also working with new FY2027 customers on potential quantum-dot applications, while selectively pursuing biomedical, photovoltaic, anti-counterfeiting, quantum and niche display opportunities.

Scale-Up Capability Remains In-House

Despite years of headcount reductions, Nanoco said it has retained the facilities and expertise needed for internal scale-up. Management pointed to previous experience scaling and validating first-generation materials with a European customer as evidence of that capability.

Potential Route to Breakeven

Management outlined a potential path to cash flow breakeven at roughly £5 million of revenue in about two years. The proposed progression runs from current contract revenue of £600,000 to £1 million, £2 million and £4 million, without a significant expansion of the cost base.

AI Exploration Begins in Research

Nanoco’s finance department is already using artificial intelligence extensively, while researchers are discussing how it could shorten the feedback loop in development work. The company is still assessing practical uses rather than presenting AI as a material near-term earnings driver.

Cash Balance Falls

Cash ended FY2026 at £9.3 million, down from £14.0 million a year earlier. The £4.7 million decline reflects continued cash burn and underlines the importance of converting development programs into commercial revenue.

Litigation and Review Costs Weighed on Results

Items below EBITDA totaled £4.3 million, including £3.7 million of litigation costs, £0.5 million for the strategic review and £0.1 million of restructuring. Litigation linked to LG cost about £0.3 million, while the Shoei proceedings generated significant discovery expenses.

Higher Depreciation Included an Impairment

Depreciation and amortization increased to £2.0 million from the prior year. The rise was largely caused by a one-off impairment of right-of-use assets with one year remaining on their associated lease term.

No New Display Licensing Deals Identified

Nanoco said it currently sees no further reasonable opportunities to claim damages from other potential display infringers, though it will continue monitoring the market. Management also does not presently see a large licensing opportunity in display technology.

Delisting Proposal Withdrawn

Indicative voting and relatively low turnout suggested that a proposed delisting resolution was unlikely to pass. The meeting was adjourned indefinitely and the resolution was withdrawn after the Board concluded that shareholders wanted Nanoco to remain listed.

Strategy Communication Needs Improvement

The shareholder consultation found that 42% of respondents did not clearly understand Nanoco’s strategy. Only 39% had watched the previous Investor Meet Company presentation, highlighting the challenge of improving engagement through webinars and live question-and-answer sessions.

Adoption and Timing Are Major Risks

Management identified customer delay or nonadoption as the company’s key business risk, a concern also cited by 70% of shareholder respondents. Commercialization involves complex devices and long supply chains, while adoption and timing are largely controlled by customers rather than Nanoco.

Customer Concentration Remains a Concern

Nanoco acknowledged significant customer concentration risk, noting that it has previously suffered from relying too heavily on one relationship. The company is seeking new leads and more customers to create a broader and more resilient revenue base.

Performance Gap Versus InGaAs

Current quantum-dot sensors deliver about 30% quantum efficiency, with some results approaching 70%, compared with 80% to 90% for established InGaAs technology. Management cautioned that comparisons can vary with voltage and temperature, but performance remains an important commercialization hurdle.

Scale-Up Timing Remains Uncertain

Management could not give a firm timetable for when the major Asian customer would move beyond scale-up, saying the process takes as long as it takes. Demand at the time of the presentation was broadly in line with the prior year, although an increase was expected over the following six months and beyond.

Forward Guidance Points to Gradual Growth

Nanoco’s FY2027 opening order book is £6.2 million, while monthly gross cash costs are expected to remain near £0.3 million to £0.4 million and planned device and IP investment totals about £0.2 million. Management expects Asian material demand to rise as the first customer approaches production, with cash flow breakeven targeted at about £5 million of revenue in roughly two years.

Nanoco’s call combined improved finances and a stronger commercial platform with a clear warning that meaningful adoption may take time. Investors have a leaner business, substantial order-book support and a potential breakeven route to watch, but must weigh those positives against cash burn, execution risk and the gap between promising technology and volume sales.

data.title: McEwen Mining Earnings Call: Recovery Meets Risk
data.description:
McEwen Mining Inc ((MUX)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

McEwen Mining’s third-quarter call carried a mixed but candid tone. Management called the quarter difficult and unacceptable, citing operational issues, higher costs, weather disruption and uncommitted construction financing, while pointing to improving October results, strong liquidity, Los Azules progress and a plan to double gold output by 2030.

Gold Production Target Remains Intact

McEwen Mining said it remains on track to double gold production by 2030. The company is targeting annual output of 250,000 to 300,000 ounces, despite the execution challenges exposed during the third quarter.

Gold Bar Returns to Positive Cash Flow

Gold Bar recorded its highest monthly production in 15 months during October and returned to positive cash flow. Management expects output of about 3,000 gold equivalent ounces per month through November and December, with early budgeting pointing to a similar monthly average in 2027.

Fox Complex Costs Improve

Costs at the Fox Complex returned within guidance in October after elevated third-quarter all-in sustaining costs. Management expects costs to remain within guidance and decline as operations shift toward the Stock Mine.

Stock Mine Could Lift Profitability

Stock is entering its ore zone and is expected to outperform Froome, helped by higher recoveries, no royalty, no haulage to the mill and roughly 30% more milling capacity from softer rock. The benefits are expected to begin in December and strengthen in early 2027.

Portfolio Moves Toward Longer-Life Mines

The company is transitioning from shorter-life operations to a longer-life portfolio. Stock is expected to operate for 8.5 to 9 years, Grey Fox for about 15 years, while Gold Bar could expand from a three- to four-year mine life to more than a decade with Trinity, Windfall and Lookout; the Mexico mill could run for 10 to 20 years, depending on permits.

Los Azules Engineering Advances

Engineering cost estimates and the execution plan for Los Azules remain on track for completion around year-end. Metso has begun work on major process plant packages, four international firms bid for the EPCM contract and bid evaluation is expected before year-end, with a final investment decision and full financing targeted for mid-2027.

Feasibility Study Offers Potential Upside

An updated Los Azules feasibility study is targeted for February 2027. It will incorporate better-than-expected geotechnical results, a higher long-term copper price based on analyst consensus and current costs from recent bids, while management sees potential for more copper and a longer mine life.

Permitting Reaches Key Milestones

Los Azules received approval to connect to Argentina’s national grid, permits for its 3,000-bed construction camp and Candadito camp, and approval to explore the neighboring Marisa I property. Basic engineering for the power line and substation is complete and ready for tender, leaving the water concession as the main outstanding permit.

Liquidity Supports Los Azules Work

Commitments under McEwen Copper’s term loan facility rose to $240 million in August. At quarter-end, McEwen Copper held $157.8 million in cash and equivalents and $138.9 million in working capital, while McEwen Mining had $49 million in cash and $10 million in marketable securities, followed by $55 million raised from selling noncore profits in October.

Resource Base Provides Scale

McEwen reported 5.8 million ounces of gold resources across all categories. Management described Los Azules as equivalent to a 56 million-ounce gold deposit on a gold-equivalent basis, with attractive costs and additional technical work expected to produce results in early 2027.

Safety and Community Support Remain Strong

Los Azules completed the third quarter without a reportable incident or lost-time injury. A survey of 2,529 residents in 10 nearby communities found that 97% accepted the project and 90% trusted it, while local suppliers received $27.7 million in business from 2023 through mid-2026.

San Jose Recovery Expected

Management expects San Jose to recover much of its lost production in the fourth quarter and meet its annual guidance. A return to clay material should improve grades, while recoveries are expected to return to first- and second-quarter levels after the operation recently achieved strong throughput following its mill expansion.

El Gallo Mill Construction Starts

Earthworks have begun for the El Gallo mill, marking the start of construction activity. Spending is expected to be modest in the fourth quarter and become more consistent in the first half of 2027 after EPCM contracts are finalized, with costs capitalized as the project advances.

Management Labels Quarter Unacceptable

Management openly described the third quarter as very difficult and unacceptable. It emphasized that McEwen, as a mining and gold company, must generate profits, but did not do so during the period.

Gold Bar Faced Management Problems

Gold Bar’s problems began in the second quarter and continued into the third, including weak oversight, insufficient detail and delayed decisions. Personnel changes have been made, although management said a heap-leach operation needs time before those changes translate into higher output.

Fox AISC Was Distorted by Development Costs

Fox Complex AISC rose because development costs for incremental ore were concentrated in the third quarter rather than spread across the remaining six to nine months of mining. Feeding the mill from a low-grade stockpile, due to excess capacity, also pushed costs higher.

Snowfall Hurt San Jose Output

Record snowfall in Argentina and Chile increased moisture at the San Jose mill and created plant problems. The operation used lower-grade, sulfide-rich stockpiles, reducing gold and silver recoveries while lowering production and increasing costs.

Los Azules Access Delay Raises Schedule Risk

The Andes experienced its heaviest snowfall in more than two decades, delaying the reopening of the Los Azules access road. Road crews expect to reach the site in early 2027, although snowmelt and spring weather could delay that further and push site work behind schedule.

First Copper Target Has Several Conditions

Los Azules continues to target first copper in 2030, but management stressed that the date depends on site access, the selected recovery measures, completion of investment decision work, project financing and customary approvals. The statement highlights the execution risk surrounding the development timetable.

Construction Financing Remains Uncommitted

Potential construction funding sources include senior project debt, strategic-investor equity at the McEwen Copper level and a possible initial public offering of McEwen Copper. Management emphasized that none of these financing sources is committed at present.

Future Equity Could Dilute Ownership

Any new equity would be raised at the McEwen Copper level. If McEwen Mining does not participate, its current 46.3% ownership stake would decline, although the size of any reduction depends on the eventual debt level and equity price.

Diesel Costs Lifted Gold Bar Expenses

Higher diesel prices increased Gold Bar’s third-quarter cash costs by approximately $200 per ounce. Management said the effect at other operations was $50 per ounce or less and was not material.

San Jose Dividends Pause in 2026

McEwen does not expect further San Jose dividends during the rest of 2026. Closure obligations are substantially or fully met, however, and additional dividends are expected in 2027 unless significant capital development follows a discovery.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management reaffirmed its goal of 250,000 to 300,000 ounces of gold production by 2030, with Gold Bar expected to sustain October-like output and Fox costs moving lower. Los Azules remains targeted for first copper in 2030, a feasibility study in February 2027 and fully financed FID in mid-2027, while San Jose is expected to deliver a strong fourth quarter and El Gallo spending should increase in the first half of 2027.

McEwen Mining’s call showed a company trying to rebuild operational credibility after a poor quarter. Improving mine performance, a sizable resource base and progress at Los Azules offer upside, but financing, weather, permitting and execution risks remain central for investors.
